newsitem.title: CHINA: China B shares down on profit-taking, A shares up.
newsitem.headline: China B shares down on profit-taking, A shares up.

text.p: China's hard currency B shares fell on profit-taking on Tuesday but domestic currency A shares fared better to record rises in both Shanghai and Shenzhen.
Shanghai's foreign currency B shares ended down slightly on Tuesday as investors took profits after a two percent rise in the index on Monday, brokers said.
"The market is taking a breather after a few days of galloping up," said an analyst at a European securities firm in Shanghai.
The Shanghai B share index fell 0.041 points, or 0.05 percent, to 77.332 points on volume of 8.567 million shares worth $5.262 million.
B shares fell after failing to break resistance at 78 points, brokers said. The absence of major foreign buying also caused the market's climb to run out of steam, they said.
Some investors also pulled money out of the market in anticipation of a new share issue, brokers said.
Shanghai Zhenhua Port Machinery Co Ltd said on Monday it had fixed the price of its 100 million B share issue at $0.433 per share, and the stock would be offered from Tuesday to Thursday.
Of 45 B shares, 39 traded with 22 down, 13 up and four flat.
Hua Xin Cement Co was the biggest B share loser on speculative selling, tumbling $0.014, or 8.14 percent, to $0.158.
Shanghai's domestic currency A shares rose more than one percent on institutional buying, brokers said.
The Shanghai A share index closed up 15.460 points, or 1.25 percent, to 1,254.720 points on volume of 535.615 million shares worth 6.397 billion yuan.
Shenzhen's hard currency B share index ended lower on Tuesday, driven down by profit-taking after a rebound in the past three sessions, brokers said.
The index lost 1.44 points, or 1.07 percent, to 132.81 points on turnover of HK$56 million, down from Monday's HK$73 million.
"Foreign institutional investors were seen cashing in on the B share market's recent gains," an analyst at J&A Securities (HK) Ltd said. "B share turnover remained thin, showing cautious sentiment."
In the B share market, newcomer Bengang Steel Plates was the most actively traded issue on volume of 2.82 million shares, losing HK$0.03 to HK$2.21.

Shenzhen's domestic A share index recovered early losses to end up 2.21 points, or 0.54 percent, at 413.23 points due to heavy selective buying of companies expected to report healthy 1997 interim earnings, brokers said.
Turnover in the A share market was seven billion yuan against 7.8 billion yuan on Monday.
Brokers said the A share market advance was helped in part by the recent slowdown in market expansion, which had resulted in less funds being diverted from listed shares.

Slight optimism, mixed with some caution over listed firms' first-half 1997 earnings, was likely to make Shenzhen's A and B share indices a bit volatile in the early stages of China's interim reporting season, brokers said.
China's corporate interim reporting season started at the beginning of July and ends on August 31.
